items.new: Before leaving the Sperm Whale's head for now, I want you, as a sensible physiologist, simply — and particularly — to take note of its front, in all its compact concentration. I want you to examine it now with the single aim of forming for yourself some unexaggerated, intelligent estimate of whatever battering-ram power may be lodged there. This is a vital point, for you must either settle this matter to your own satisfaction, or remain forever an unbeliever about one of the most appalling, but no less true, events to be found perhaps anywhere in all recorded history.

items.new: You observe that in the ordinary swimming position of the Sperm Whale, the front of his head presents an almost entirely vertical surface to the water. You observe that the lower part of that front slopes considerably backward, so as to leave more room for the long socket that receives the boom-like lower jaw. You observe that the mouth is entirely under the head, much as though your own mouth were entirely under your chin. Moreover, you observe that the whale has no external nose, and that what nose he has — his spout hole — is on the top of his head; you observe that his eyes and ears are at the sides of his head, nearly one third of his entire length back from the front. So you must by now have realized that the front of the Sperm Whale's head is a dead, blind wall, without a single organ or tender projection of any kind whatsoever. Furthermore, you must now consider that only in the extreme, lower, backward-sloping part of the front of the head is there the slightest trace of bone, and that not until you get nearly twenty feet back from the forehead do you come to the full development of the skull. So this whole enormous boneless mass is like one wad. Finally, although, as will soon be revealed, its contents partly consist of the most delicate oil, you must now be told the nature of the substance that so impregnably encases all that apparent delicacy. Earlier I described to you how the blubber wraps the body of the whale as the rind wraps an orange. It is just the same with the head, but with this difference: around the head this envelope, though not so thick, has a boneless toughness that no one who has not handled it can imagine. The most sharply pointed harpoon, the keenest lance thrown by the strongest human arm, bounces off it powerlessly. It is as though the forehead of the Sperm Whale were paved with horses' hoofs. I do not think that any sensation lurks in it.

items.new: Think of another thing, too. When two large, loaded Indiamen — big merchant ships of the India trade — happen to crowd and crush toward each other in the docks, what do the sailors do? They do not hang between them, at the point where they will touch, any merely hard substance, like iron or wood. No, they hold there a large, round wad of tow (coarse hemp fiber) and cork, wrapped in the thickest and toughest of ox-hide. That wad bravely and without injury takes the squeeze that would have snapped all their oak handspikes and iron crowbars. By itself this is enough to illustrate the obvious fact I am driving at. But in addition to this, it has occurred to me as a hypothesis that, since ordinary fish have what is called a swimming bladder, which they can swell or shrink at will; and since the Sperm Whale, as far as I know, has no such equipment; considering, too, the otherwise unaccountable way in which he sometimes sinks his head completely beneath the surface, and at other times swims with it raised high out of the water; considering the unobstructed elasticity of its envelope; considering the unique interior of his head — it has occurred to me as a hypothesis, I say, that those mystical, lung-celled honeycombs in there may possibly have some hitherto unknown and unsuspected connection with the outer air, so that they can be swelled and shrunk by the atmosphere. If this is so, imagine the irresistible force of that might, when the most impalpable and destructive of all the elements contributes to it.
